target_problem: target-compatible excess-overlap at most one for a fixed opposite-phase signed-MUX first pair after the V113 common-dominator optimum-face decomposition
conditional_implication: if every non-common V113 dominator stage is acyclic, then target-compatible overlap at most minimum_overlap+1 is decidable in polynomial time by a one-budget extension of the V113 phase DP using independent prefix/suffix gate flows around the unique extra shared gate
current_gap: the theorem requires every non-common dominator stage to be acyclic; no argument shows this structural condition is universal, and V114 shows that unrestricted directed extra-gate completion already contains a two-linkage hardness barrier
stop_rule: do not extend the DAG proof to cyclic stages without an explicit bounded interface parameter or a new structural lemma; V116 must parameterize cyclic interaction or prove hardness at the first cyclic level
external_validation_target: Tholey 2012 DAG two-disjoint-path tractability, Fortune-Hopcroft-Wyllie 1980 general directed linkage hardness, and specialist review of the signed-MUX dominator-stage transfer
bridge_lemmas: V113 minimum overlap equals the number of common gate dominators
an overlap budget of minimum+1 permits at most one non-common shared gate
in an acyclic dominator stage no output gate can occur both before and after the unique extra shared gate without creating a directed cycle
fixed extra gate and branch choices therefore factor into two gate-disjoint prefix and suffix flow problems
signed target compatibility at common gates and the extra gate is determined by local successor source phases
a constant phase state plus one excess-budget bit gives a polynomial dynamic program
the exact-stretch family n=8+t, m=9+t has minimum overlap one and minimum compatible overlap two for every t>=0
